observations: Cross-chain, nothing stood out: no requests on the Unichain vault since the 2026-11-18 evidence programme, and no freeze or callback activity on Ethereum Sepolia either (its recent history cannot be re-read — the public RPC has pruned that range — so this rests on the absence of observed events, not a full rescan). The request arrived at 12:01 JST, an unremarkable hour for this vault. The model's same-chain view missed none of this, because there was nothing to miss.
rationale: This request was vetoed (MEDIUM) almost entirely because of timing, not amount or destination. It was the vault's first withdrawal request in about 61 hours — roughly five times the profile's median interval — and the model treats the first move after a long silence as the moment a stolen key would act (interval_log 1.80 is the dominant feature). Everything else is quiet: the amount is small (0.001 ETH, about 9% of the vault balance), the destination is the owner's own long-known address (first_seen 0), and there is no burst pattern — no other requests in the last hour or the last day. A single MEDIUM vetoes only this request and freezes nothing; the same request made a day later, with the interval back to normal, scores LOW and executes.

observations: Cross-chain, nothing stood out: the Unichain vault's only recorded request remains the 2026-11-18 evidence-programme one, and all three vaults were verified unfrozen at the start of this run. Ethereum Sepolia's persisted history is empty and its cursor is stale relative to its head, and the worker log shows its public RPC reporting the early range as pruned, so that chain's recent activity could not be fully re-read and this note rests on the absence of observed events there. The request arrived at 12:43 JST, the usual midday heartbeat hour, and its destination, the owner, is also the destination recorded in the Unichain history.
rationale: This request scored LOW (555), below the MEDIUM threshold of 620, and was executed as a routine daily withdrawal. The largest feature is interval_log 1.12, reflecting a gap of 24.64 hours since the previous request, longer than a day but well short of the silence that drove the previous verdict higher. Everything else is quiet: amount_ratio 0.10 and balance_ratio 0.09 show a small amount relative to both the profile and the vault balance, first_seen 0.0 shows the destination is the owner's known address, and there were no other requests in the preceding hour or day. With no feature at an anomalous level, the request executed and the vault balance was then restored by a matching deposit.
